Based on the provided context, when a spell or ability instructs creatures to fight, each of those creatures deals damage equal to its power to the other creature (rule 701.14a). This damage is not combat damage (rule 701.14d). If a creature fights itself, it deals damage to itself equal to twice its power (rule 701.14c). 

However, if one or both of the creatures are no longer on the battlefield, are no longer creatures, or are illegal targets for a resolving spell or ability that instructs them to fight, neither of them fights or deals damage (rule 701.14b).

Based on the provided context, the cleanup step is used for the following turn-based actions and events:

* The active player discards cards if their hand contains more cards than their maximum hand size (Rule 514.1).
* All damage marked on permanents (including phased-out permanents) is removed, and all "until end of turn" and "this turn" effects end (Rule 514.2).
* If state-based actions need to be performed and/or triggered abilities are waiting to be put onto the stack (including those triggering "at the beginning of the next cleanup step" or during the process of ending turns and phases), those actions are performed and those abilities are put on the stack, giving the active player priority to cast spells and activate abilities, followed by another cleanup step (Rules 514.3a, 724.1f).
